Listening for a wake word means the microphone stays on in the background. Android shows a notification the whole time, it uses battery, and some phones stop background apps anyway. JARVIS can\'t listen while the phone is off or while Android has restricted the app. It is off until you turn it on.
When on, JARVIS runs a visible foreground service. Turn it off any time here or from its notification.
After a restart, remind me to resume
Android 14+ doesn\'t let apps start the microphone by themselves after a restart, so JARVIS shows a notification you can tap.
Allow unrestricted use so Android doesn\'t stop listening
Detection runs on this phone. Higher sensitivity catches more but mishears more.
Automatic uses the on-device model when it is installed, otherwise Android\'s speech service if it can run on the device, otherwise it asks you to download the model
Raise it if JARVIS misses you; lower it if it wakes by mistake
Used by the Android speech service method. The on-device model always listens for “hey jarvis”. Separate several with commas.
Each wake word needs at least two letters.

The island is a small bar JARVIS draws over other apps. Android doesn\'t tell apps where the camera hole physically is. JARVIS uses the display-cutout information Android reports and, if there is none, sits at the top centre. Use the position and offsets below to line it up.
Required by Android for anything drawn over other apps
Shows a short demo on the island
The island isn\'t running. Turn it on first.
Android wouldn\'t start the island. Open JARVIS again and retry; if it keeps failing, check the log in Diagnostics.
Automatic follows the cutout Android reports. You can also drag the island itself to move it.
Where it sits along the top edge

This is a policy for what JARVIS may do while the phone is locked. JARVIS never unlocks the phone, skips the lock, or weakens it. Anything private makes it ask you to unlock with your own PIN, pattern or fingerprint.
Allow JARVIS on the lock screen
Off: everything except harmless requests asks you to unlock
How much may be shown or done while locked
Strict (recommended): only harmless things such as the time, timers, volume and general questions work while locked. Everything personal asks you to unlock.
Balanced: also allows the items you switch on below. Calls ask for confirmation first. Messages and anything that opens another app still need unlock.

Open: personal reads such as notes and reminders are allowed while locked if you turned lock-screen mode on. Anyone holding your phone could ask for them. Only choose this on a phone nobody else touches.
These only apply when lock-screen mode is on, and some only at the Balanced or Open level.
Save notes and reminders by voice
You can add things; reading them back still needs unlock
Needs notification access and the Balanced or Open level
Otherwise calls work only with a spoken number
Lets an alarm-style reminder light up a locked screen
Time and date, timers, volume, torch, general questions, saving a dictated note (if allowed).
Placing a call (if allowed). You confirm by tapping or saying yes.
Reading notes, reminders, contacts or notifications; opening apps; messages; settings. Android\'s own unlock screen appears and JARVIS continues only after you unlock.
Bypassing, skipping or disabling the lock. Reading your PIN or biometrics. Anything on a phone that has been rebooted and not yet unlocked once.

Designed from Android\'s public lock-screen rules and not tested on a real device here. Some phone makers limit what apps can show over the lock screen or stop background apps, so behaviour can differ.

Android asks for each of these separately. Granting one never switches another on, and every feature below is off until you turn it on. JARVIS keeps recent notifications in memory only, and nothing is saved to disk.
Notification access lets JARVIS know what is playing, read notifications to you when you ask, and use a notification\'s own Reply button.
System permission; opens Android\'s own screen
Needed for \"what\'s playing?\" and \"read my notifications\"
Only when the phone is unlocked and nothing private is hidden by your lock-screen settings
Reply to chat messages from their notification
WhatsApp and other apps that show a Reply button

Replies use the app\'s own notification Reply action, so JARVIS never reads or types into the chat app itself. JARVIS always shows you the message and asks before sending, and it only says \"sent\" when Android reports the reply went out.

Disclosure: this uses Android\'s accessibility service only to press Home, Back, Recents, open the notification shade or quick settings, lock the screen, take a screenshot or open the power menu when you ask. It does not read what is on the screen, watch what you type, or see other apps\' content.
Turn it on in Android\'s accessibility settings
Without it, \"go home\" and \"open recents\" explain that they need it

Notes, exported chats, generated images and documents are saved here. Changing this only affects new files; existing ones stay where they are. After a reinstall Android no longer lets JARVIS list files it saved earlier in Documents; they are still in the Files app.
Documents/JARVIS is visible in the Files app; private storage is only visible to JARVIS and is removed when you uninstall
Browse, share, save a copy or delete

Where API keys are kept, encrypted

Time and reminder parsing, request routing, the \"did it really work?\" checks, storage rules, contact matching, the island geometry and the database queries are covered by automated tests on a computer.

Alarms, background listening, the island overlay, the lock-screen flow, voice recognition quality, wake-word accuracy, secure key storage across phone makers and live AI providers depend on your phone and accounts. They have not been verified on a device by whoever built this. If something misbehaves, the log below helps.
The log contains events and error types only. API keys, tokens and message text are removed before anything is written. Read it before sharing it.

A personal assistant that lives on your phone: it keeps reminders, notes and timers, makes calls, opens apps, controls the device, answers questions, writes, and creates images. It tells you plainly when it can\'t do something or when it couldn\'t confirm that it worked.
Your messages go to the AI provider you set up
Groq, Cohere, OpenAI or your own Ollama server, only if you added a key or address. Reminders and notes are included only when the setting allows it.
Speech goes to Android\'s speech service
Depending on your phone, Google\'s or the manufacturer\'s service may process it in the cloud. JARVIS does not store audio. You can ask for on-device recognition in Voice settings.
Web searches go to SerpAPI (with a key) or DuckDuckGo; the weather city goes to Open-Meteo; image prompts go to Pollinations or Hugging Face.
Reminders, notes, timers, conversation history, contacts (looked up locally), settings and encrypted keys.
JARVIS has no advertising or analytics, and no crash reporting service. Nothing is uploaded unless you ask for something that needs a service above.

The on-device detector is three small neural-network files (about %1$s MB) from the openWakeWord project on GitHub. JARVIS downloads them only when you tap Download, checks each one against a fixed checksum, and keeps them private to this app. The detector listens for the phrase “hey jarvis”; the wake words you type below only apply to the Android speech service method.
These models are licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: free for non-commercial use only. Source: github.com/dscripka/openWakeWord

If a permission below is greyed out or says "Restricted setting", Android is blocking apps installed from a file. Open App info, tap the three-dot menu at the top right, choose "Allow restricted settings", then come back and grant the permission.
